quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, you should:

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not on your surroundings.

questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes you more visible to other drivers and reduces your risk of a collision. Always watch other drivers and be ready for their movements.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard for drivers to see your motorcycle's turn signals, you should:

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell other drivers about upcoming turns.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when sunlight makes your mechanical signals hard to see. It is very important to clearly communicate with other drivers.

questions.question: You have a better chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best defense against injury while riding. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield can protect your face in a crash.

questions.question: Your motorcycle should fit you. This means:

options.text: Your fingertips should barely reach the handlebars when you are seated.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when you are standing next to the motorcycle.
Your feet should comfortably reach the ground when you are seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should comfortably reach the ground when you are seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you correctly if your feet comfortably reach the ground while you sit on it. Make sure a motorcycle fits you before you ride.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can cause permanent hearing damage. Use ear protection when you ride to protect your hearing while still being able to hear important sounds like sirens or car horns.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Brightly-colored clothing to increase your visibility.
Clothing of any color because other drivers can easily see you in daylight.
Dark-colored clothing to contrast with the bright sunlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brightly-colored clothing to increase your visibility.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in broad daylight. Always wear brightly-colored clothing to increase your visibility when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white signs with red and black markings. They inform drivers of specific traffic laws. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Eye protection:

options.text: Is not necessary if your motorcycle has a windshield.
Is only necessary when riding in bad weather.
Should allow you to see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should allow you to see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: Face and eye protection is required by law in California. A face shield protects your whole face in a crash. A good eye or face shield must allow you to see clearly to both sides.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time, you should:

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is the best way.
Just start riding. Most bikes are the same, so you don't need to learn the bike first.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding to learn how the bike works.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, learn how it operates. Check the safety and maintenance, find where everything is located, and practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to understand how it works.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle's transmission must be in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that turns on when the ignition is on and the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: Unlike other substances, alcohol:

options.text: Must be digested before entering the bloodstream.

questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine into the bloodstream. This happens quickly and affects the brain fast.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane to see around vehicles ahead.
Ride close to the vehicle in front to use their headlights.
Slow down to help you avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to help you avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slower than you would during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your following distance and stay flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like car mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like car mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you stay balanced.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work properly.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test each brake control to make sure it lights up the brake lights.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When a tailgater is following you, you should:

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in a way that helps the tailgater pass you. Going faster will only make them tailgate at higher speeds, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: How can you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: The only way to become sober is to wait for your body to remove the alcohol. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has white background with red and black markings. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: How can you prevent fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Limit your riding to a few hours each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit your riding to a few hours each day.
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks to rest, even if you don't feel tired. Do not ride more than six hours per day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tired faster. Dress well to protect yourself from the weather.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Do not wear dark or dull colors while riding.

questions.question: When is there less traction available for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is straight up and down.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, such as when turning, there is less grip available for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.
